questions.question: Which of the following cell divisions is known as reduction division?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meiosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meiosis**:-

 
 
• **It is known as reduction division because it reduces the number of chromosomes in a cell by half, resulting in four haploid daughter cells.**
 
• This process is essential for sexual reproduction as it allows for the formation of gametes with half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell, which then combine during fertilization to form a zygote with a full set of chromosomes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telophase:-**

 
 
• It is a stage in both mitosis and meiosis where the nuclear membrane reforms around the separated chromosomes, but it is not known as reduction division.
 
 
 
• **Prophase:-**
 
 
• It is the stage in both mitosis and meiosis where the chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, but it is not known as reduction division.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis:-**
 
 
• It is a type of cell division where a single cell divides into two identical daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
 
• It does not involve a reduction in chromosome number and is not known as reduction division.

questions.question: Under which of the following Articles of the Indian constitution "Equality of opportunities include its reasonable classification and provisions for backward class of citizens" is provided.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 16.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 16:- Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.**

 
 
• This article guarantees equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters of public employment.
 
• No citizen can be discriminated against on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence, or any of them.
 
• However, the state can make special provisions for the backward classes, under-represented states, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes for posts under the state.
 
• Local candidates may also be given preference in certain posts. Reservation of posts for people of a certain religion or denomination in a religious or denominational institution is not illegal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 17: Abolition of Untouchability**

 
 
• This article prohibits the practice of untouchability and makes it an offense punishable by law. Untouchability is considered a social stigma and a form of discrimination against people based on their caste.
 
 
 
• **Article 18: ****Abolition of titles:** No title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the State.
 
 
• 
 Article 18 of the Indian Constitution prohibits the conferment and acceptance of titles by the State and its citizens, except in the cases of military or academic distinctions.
 
 
• 
 It bars Indian citizens from accepting titles from foreign states.
 
 
 
 
• **Article 19: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.**
 
 
• This article guarantees certain fundamental rights to all citizens, including the right to freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, and residence. However, these rights are subject to reasonable restrictions in the interests of the general public.

questions.question: Who is credited with setting up of Brahmo Sabha, for religious reforms, in 1828, which was later called Brahma Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy:-**

 
 
• **He is credited with setting up of Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which later became known as Brahma Samaj.**
 
• He was a social reformer who advocated for the abolition of practices such as Sati and child marriage. 
 
• Roy's efforts towards religious and social reform paved the way for the Indian Renaissance.
 
 
 
• **Brahma Samaj:-**
 
 
• It was founded as a monotheistic Hindu reform movement that emphasized the worship of one God and the rejection of idol worship.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabindranath Tagore:-**

 
 
• He was a poet, writer, and philosopher who was associated with the Indian independence movement.
 
• While he was a follower of the Brahma Samaj and was influenced by Raja Ram Mohan Roy's ideas, he was not involved in setting up the movement.
 
 
 
• **Keshub Chandra Sen:-**
 
 
• Keshub Chandra Sen was a disciple of Raja Ram Mohan Roy and played a significant role in the development of the Brahma Samaj.
 
• He later broke away from the Brahma Samaj and founded his own movement, the Brahmo Samaj of India.
 
 
 
• **Devendra Nath Tagore:-**
 
 
• Devendra Nath Tagore was a follower of Raja Ram Mohan Roy and played an important role in the development of the Brahma Samaj.
 
• He was the father of Rabindranath Tagore and was a prominent figure in the Bengal Renaissance.

questions.question: Which physicist is known for discovering that any periodic wave can be represented as an infinite number of weighted sinusoids, i.e., the sum of sine and cosine waves?

__
 
• **Jean Baptiste Joseph Fourier:-**

 
 
• **The physicist known for discovering that any periodic wave can be represented as an infinite number of weighted sinusoids is Jean Baptiste Joseph Fourier.**
 
• This discovery is known as the Fourier series or Fourier transform.
 
• Fourier's work has had a significant impact on fields such as mathematics, physics, and engineering.
 
• The Fourier series is used in signal processing to analyze and manipulate signals, such as those in audio and video processing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Louis de Broglie:-**

 
 
• He was a physicist known for his work on the wave-particle duality of matter.
 
 
 
• **Joseph-Louis Lagrange:-**
 
 
• He was a mathematician and physicist known for his contributions to mechanics and the calculus of variations.
 
 
 
• **Ernest Walton:-**
 
 
• He was a physicist known for his work on the splitting of the atom and the development of the first particle accelerator.

questions.question: The cropping season between Rabi and Kharif is called ___________.

__
 
• **Zaid:-**

 
 
• **It is a short-duration cropping season that falls between the Rabi and Kharif seasons.**
 
• It is typically practiced in regions with mild winters and hot summers, such as in the northern plains of India.
 
• Crops that are typically grown during the Zaid season include watermelon, cucumber, muskmelon, and vegetables like okra, pumpkin, and bitter gourd.
 
• The Zaid season is important as it allows farmers to utilize their land more efficiently and increase their overall productivity by growing crops during the off-season.

• It is a monsoon season crop that is sown in May-June and harvested in November-December.
 
 
 
• **Boro:-**
 
 
• It is a winter season crop that is sown in November-December and harvested in April-May.
 
 
 
• **Aus:-**
 
 
• It is a summer season crop that is sown in May-June and harvested in September-October.

questions.question:
While using the income method to compute national income, which of the following is NOT to be included?

A) Income from lottery

B) Brokerage on sale and purchase of shares

C) Income from illegal activities like gambling
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A and C.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Income method:-**

 
 
• It is one of the methods used to calculate national income.
 
• It involves adding up all the incomes earned by individuals and businesses in the economy. 
 
 
 
• **Lottery income:-**
 
 
• It is considered a windfall gain and is not a regular source of income.
 
• It is not a productive activity and does not contribute to the production of goods and services in the economy.
 
• Therefore, income from lottery is not included while calculating national income using the income method.
 
 
 
• **Brokerage on sale and purchase of shares:-**
 
 
• Brokerage income is earned by individuals or firms that facilitate the buying and selling of shares in the stock market.
 
• This income is a result of productive activity and is included while calculating national income using the income method.
 
 
 
• **Income from illegal activities like gambling:-**
 
 
• Income earned from illegal activities like gambling is not included in the calculation of national income.
 
• Such activities are not recognized by the government and are not considered productive activities that contribute to the economy

questions.question: Which of these is NOT part of the classification of economic activities carried out in an economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Law and order.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Economic activities:-**

 
 
• **The classification of economic activities is an important aspect of understanding the functioning of an economy.**
 
• The main categories of economic activities include production, consumption, and distribution.
 
• Production refers to the creation of goods and services, while consumption involves the use of these goods and services by individuals and businesses.
 
• Distribution refers to the movement of goods and services from producers to consumers, including transportation, storage, and marketing.
 
• **Law and order, on the other hand, is not a part of the classification of economic activities, as it pertains to the maintenance of social order and the enforcement of laws, rather than economic production and consumption.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Production**:

 
 
• This category includes all activities related to the creation of goods and services, such as manufacturing, agriculture, mining, and construction.
 
 
 
• **Consumption**:
 
 
• This category includes all activities related to the use of goods and services by individuals and businesses, such as household spending, business investment, and government consumption.
 
 
 
• **Distribution**:
 
 
• This category includes all activities related to the movement of goods and services from producers to consumers, such as transportation, storage, and marketing. It also includes activities related to the allocation of resources, such as pricing and market research.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the fall out of the industrial licensing system?

options.text: Large industrial houses availed licenses to prevent competition
Most licenses were used up by backward states
Most licenses were for importing goods
Many small private firms appropriated licenses

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Large industrial houses availed licenses to prevent competition.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The industrial licensing system in India had several fallout, including:**

 
 
• Large industrial houses availed licenses to prevent competition: The licensing system was often manipulated by big business houses to prevent new players from entering the market, thereby limiting competition.
 
• Most licenses were used up by backward states: The licensing system favored the established industrial centers, and backward states had a tough time getting licenses.
 
• Most licenses were for importing goods: The licensing system was designed to promote domestic manufacturing, and imports were discouraged.
 
• Many small private firms appropriated licenses: The licensing system was biased towards large industrial houses, and small private firms had a tough time getting licenses. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial licensing system:**

 
 
• The industrial licensing system was introduced in India in 1948 to regulate the growth and development of industries in the country.
 
• Under this system, the government issued licenses to companies to set up new industries, expand existing ones, or import technology and machinery.
 
• The licensing system was aimed at achieving a balanced regional development of industries, promoting self-sufficiency, and preventing concentration of economic power in a few hands.
 
• However, the licensing system was often criticized for being bureaucratic, corrupt, and favoring established players over new entrants.
 
• The system was gradually dismantled in the 1990s as part of economic liberalization and reforms.
